full_judgment:
Md. Fazlul Haque J:- This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 4.11.2002 passed by the Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9363 of 2002. 

 2. The respondent Delwar Hossain Talukder as an accused in G. R Case No. 545 of 2014 pending to the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class Shariatpur moved unsuccessfully the learned Sessions Judge, Shariatpur for bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 153 of 2002. Thereafter, Delwar Hossain Talukder as petitioner moved the High Court Division whereby Rule was obtained in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9363 and the same was made absolute by the learned Judges of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 4.11.2002 enlarging the present respondent on bail. Against the order of bail, the appellant as petitioner filed criminal petition for leave to appeal and the leave was granted to consider that in view of the fact as stated in the F. I. R. that Delwar Hossain Talukder had fired gun shot at the fighting and at his instance the younger brother of informant died the High Court Division has fallen in an error of law in enlarging the respondent on bail by the impugned judgment and order dated 4.11.2002 in the case of murder under section 302 of the Penal code and as such the impugned judgment and order is required to be investigated. 

 5. It appears that 49 accused persons appeared before the High Court Division to obtain the anticipatory bail in this criminal Case. The High Court Division enlarged Col. (Retd). Shawkat Ali only on bail and directed others to surrender before the court of Magistrate within 26.9.2001. It appears that the present respondent did not surrender before the court of Magistrate, Shariatpur within 26th September, 2001, he was subsequently arrested by the police. The respondent Delwar Hossain Talukder as an accused in G. R. Case No. 545 of 2001 pending in the court of Magistrate 1St Class, Shariatpur moved unsuccessfully the learned Session Judge, Shariatpur for bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 153 of 2002. Thereafter, the respondent Delwar Hossain Talukder filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9363 of 2002 whereupon the Division Bench of the High Court Division issued Rule and the same was made absolute by order dated 4.11.2002. The state moved this Division against the order dated 4.11.2002 granting bail to the accused respondent. 

 6. The F. I. R. case is that Delwar Hossain Talukder in the broad day light fired a gun shot and killed the brother of the informant. It also appears that the police has submitted charge-sheet against the respondent and others under different sections including section 302 of the Penal Code. The case as set out in the prosecution report is that the respondent has committed an offence of murder under section 302/34 of the Penal Code. Section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure speaks of that when there is a reasonable ground for believing that a person is guilty of offence publishable with death or imprisonment for life, he should not be granted bail. Section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure although is a procedural law and the accused having alleged to have committed a substantive offence of murder his liberty may be curtailed. Strictly speaking, the accused respondent is arrested for committing an offence of murder and he may be deprived of his liberty. 

 7. We are called upon to decided as to whether the Division Bench of the High Court Division was correct in enlarging the accused respondent in bail although he is a F.I.R named accused in the case of murder under section 302/34 of the Penal Code. As stated herein above in a broad day light the accused respondent had fired a gun shot aiming the deceased Delwar Hossain, the younger brother of the informant and it is the informant, who has specifically and categorically stated that the present respondent is responsible for the murder of the brother of the informant. Arguments has been advanced that before the firing started by rival groups, few cocktails were exploded and it was not possible for informant to see for himself that the accused respondent had fired gun shot at his (informants) brother. 

 9. Considering these aspects of the case we are of the view that the High Court Division has failed to exercise discretion vested in it in granting bail to the accused respondent, and we are of the view that there is merit in this appeal.
